JPMorgan's third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of $5.75 per share missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.94. After considering the net investment securities losses of 18 cents, earnings were $5.57 per share, up 9.9% from a year ago.Reported net revenues of $50.17 billion rose 8% year over year but missed the consensus mark of $52.21 billion. Strong equity trading performance, IB activity and loan growth supported revenues, while fixed income trading business was subdued.Including the significant item, net income rose 6% year over year to $15.3 billion. Markets revenues climbed 15% year over year to $10.32 billion, driven predominantly by Equity Markets. Equity Markets revenues surged 49% to $4.95 billion on strong performance across products, particularly Prime and Derivatives. However, Fixed Income Markets revenues declined 4% to $5.37 billion, reflecting weakness in Commodities, Rates, Credit and Public Finance, partly offset by Currencies and Emerging Markets.Investment Banking revenues increased 15% to $3.10 billion, largely driven by higher advisory fees. Securities Services revenues increased 14% to $1.63 billion. Reported NII increased 13% year over year to $27.04 billion. The net yield on interest-earning assets improved to 2.48% from 2.45% a year earlier. Non-interest expenses increased 12% year over year to $27.30 billion. Higher compensation, brokerage and distribution fees, marketing and technology expenses drove the increase. Compensation costs reflected revenue-related payments and an expanding front-office workforce.The reported overhead ratio deteriorated to 54% from 52% a year earlier. The provision for credit losses declined 19% to $2.74 billion. Net charge-offs fell $389 million to $2.20 billion, primarily driven by Wholesale. JPM recorded a $539 million net reserve build, mainly in Wholesale. Card Services & Auto revenues advanced 15%, aided by higher card balances, improved net yield and auto leasing income. Morgan’s global head of ETFs, said: “The strategy seeks to identify attractively valued, fundamentally sound companies, with the potential to benefit as market leadership evolves.” “As Europe’s active ETF market matures, investors are increasingly looking to diversify beyond broad market exposure to consider how different investment styles can complement their portfolios.” See also: HANetf launches AI Revolution ETF with Yorkville Ives & Co Classified as Article 8 under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation, JGLV has a TER of 0.55%, and is listed on the London Stock Exchange, Deutsche Börse Xetra, Borsa Italiana, SIX Swiss Exchange. title: JPMorgan Partners With OpenAI: What It Means for JPM's AI Strategy - The Globe and Mail
content: JPMorgan’s JPM partnership with OpenAI marks another step in its efforts to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) across banking operations. Per a Finextra report, the collaboration, disclosed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman at the Nov. 4 WSJ Tech conference, will provide the banking giant access to OpenAI’s Codex coding agent and cybersecurity-focused models. The agreement aligns with the bank’s broader AI strategy of leveraging advanced technologies to enhance efficiency, accelerate innovation and strengthen operational resilience.The collaboration could accelerate JPMorgan’s technology transformation by streamlining software development and automating routine tasks. Codex will likely enable engineers to improve coding efficiency, reduce development timelines and allocate resources toward more complex projects. Broader adoption of AI-powered tools is also likely to enhance employee productivity and optimize workflows, potentially supporting operating leverage over time.Cybersecurity represents another strategic opportunity. OpenAI’s advanced models are expected to help JPMorgan strengthen threat detection, identify vulnerabilities and improve incident response capabilities. Given the bank’s extensive digital infrastructure and sensitive customer data, enhanced cybersecurity defenses will support operational resilience and reinforce customer confidence. However, AI-generated outputs will require rigorous validation and human oversight.Despite these potential benefits, the collaboration could further increase JPM’s technology-related expenses. With the bank planning to spend $19.8 billion on technology this year, additional costs associated with AI integration, computing infrastructure, employee training and ongoing model monitoring could add to its expense burden, potentially delaying the realization of meaningful efficiency gains. Moreover, data privacy concerns, regulatory scrutiny and third-party technology risks could complicate implementation across the bank’s operations.The OpenAI collaboration reinforces JPMorgan’s commitment to AI-driven transformation and will strengthen its competitive positioning through improved productivity, faster innovation and enhanced cybersecurity. However, undisclosed implementation costs, deployment timelines and expected savings leave its financial impact uncertain. Two close peers of JPMorgan are Bank of AmericaBAC and Citigroup C. Bank of America is leveraging AI to streamline operations, automate repetitive tasks and enhance employee productivity. Bank of America’s EricaAssist platform accelerates customer service, while AI-powered coding tools have improved developer productivity by more than 20%. AI-driven document processing and workflow automation further support cost savings and operational efficiency. Citigroup is leveraging AI to automate manual processes, streamline client onboarding and accelerate software development. Its AI-powered coding tools have improved product launch speeds by 30-40%, while technology vendor spending declined 30% year over year. These initiatives support cost savings, employee productivity and operational efficiency at Citigroup. JPM’s shares have gained 14.1% over the past six months. From a valuation standpoint, JPMorgan trades at a 12-month trailing price-to-tangible book (P/TB) of 3.20X, above the industry average. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for JPMorgan's 2026 earnings suggests a 22.7% year-over-year rise, while that for 2027 earnings indicates a 3.7% increase. In the past week, earnings estimates for 2026 and 2027 have remained unchanged at $24.95 and $25.87, respectively. JPMorgan currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). But the stocks everyone knows about aren't likely to keep delivering the biggest profits. AI’s second wave is moving from infrastructure to implementation and these companies are at the forefront of this transition, positioned to become what Amazon and Google were to the internet era. While the midterm election results sent a clear message that voters have concerns about the rapid data center build-out, it appears the industry's construction pipeline is still on track — at least for next year. New research from J.P. Morgan Asset Management and comments from CoreWeave leadership in the wake of its unexpectedly strong third-quarter earnings report point to a positive outlook for development in 2027, even if the sector is ultimately expected to lose steam in 2028. “We do not anticipate any impact from the seismic regulatory shift that’s occurred,” CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said during the firm’s Tuesday afternoon earnings call. “We are very comfortable with our pipeline. ... We believe that what has occurred is a statement around how you build. We want to build responsibly.” “So we think that is an opportunity for us to continue to scale our business within the new political reality that exists,” he added. The AI firm's stock had plunged last week after anti-data center candidates swept the midterms, but it has been rallying since then, including a more than 26% jump since the earnings report was released Tuesday. CoreWeave reported $3.66B in quarterly revenue, up 168% year-over-year and beating industry estimates of $3.56B. It has also raised its full-year revenue guidance. The bullish outlook aligns with a projection from J.P. Morgan, which expects artificial intelligence-related capital expenditures to reach $1.5T in 2027 and level off in the following year due to political pushback, Semafor reported. J.P. Morgan researchers said in the report that the legislative pushback to data center construction has “more bark than bite.” Of the 16 statewide moratoriums that have been proposed, just one in New York has become law. The report also found that weeding out speculative projects could be good for the industry. It said of the 430 gigawatts worth of proposed data center projects, just 59% are in active development. “Projects already under construction are generally less vulnerable to new restrictions,” J.P.
